data.title: Guidance on Coping Strategies Index indicator | IndiKit
data.content: 1) Identify the main locally relevant consumption-related coping strategies that target households use when they do not have enough food or money to buy food. Identify these strategies through focus group discussions with people from the target population. You can use the list of common strategies in the CSI Field Methods Manual (see below), or those identified by the Food Security Cluster if available, as a starting point. Adjust the list to the local context so that it includes only [...] The Coping Strategies Index (CSI) is a context-specific indicator used to assess household food-access stress by measuring the extent to which households engage in consumption-related coping strategies when they lack sufficient food or money to buy food. The indicator produces a numerical score reflecting the frequency and severity of these coping behaviours. Higher scores indicate greater use of coping strategies and therefore greater food-access stress. Compared to the Reduced Coping Strategy [...] it includes only strategies that are actually used during food-insecure periods. Do not include strategies that people do not use or that are common even when households are food secure, such as collecting wild food from the river.

data.content:
Food insecurity: Since the food security measure uses multiple items, it covers households worrying about food running out, dietary quality and variety, and quantity of food consumed. Food insecurity is measured at two levels of severity. In households with low food security, the hardships experienced are primarily reductions in dietary quality and variety. In households with very low food security, the hardships experienced are reduced food intake and skipped meals. [...] The ready availability of nutritionally adequate and safe foods.
 Assured ability to acquire acceptable foods in socially acceptable ways (that is, without resorting to emergency food supplies, scavenging, stealing, or other coping strategies).

## What Is Food Insecurity?

Food insecurity is the limited or uncertain availability of nutritionally adequate and safe foods, or limited or uncertain ability to acquire acceptable foods in socially acceptable ways. [...] Food insecure. Households that report three or more conditions that indicate food insecurity are classified as "food insecure." That is, the households were at times unable to acquire adequate food for one or more household members because they had insufficient money and other resources for food.
